text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected on dedicated-prod-pool-3 across streaming routes. p99 > 5s for last 3m, queue depth rising. Paging oncall.

mara: oncall here. seeing p95 ~1.1s p99 ~5.6s on pool-3, streaming stalls reported by client telemetry. tagging eng-runtime + eng-sre.

owen: looking. initial gauge: pool-3 GPU util 98%, enqueue depth ~420 (norm ~20). warmup success rate dropped ~70%. autoscaler not adding nodes; handshake latency to spawn workers ~45s.

liam: checking autoscaler logs, seeing warmup token timeouts and zk backpressure. autoscale decisions issued but new instances stuck in "initializing" due to image pull / warmup backlog. stacktrace: `timeout waiting for warmup` in warmup-manager.

mara: customer-impact? nina?

nina: several mid-market customers on Dedicated tier reporting streaming stalls and aborted sessions. CS ticket volume spiking. No full outages, but severe SLO degradation for streaming endpoints (users see partial streams or long stalls).

cody: flagged top-3 customers. asking for mitigation steps and ETA for manual actions. customers want status and ETA within 15m.

owen: quick mitigation plan: (1) throttle new long-stream sessions to reduce queue growth (2) enable fallback routing to hosted-inference for non-sensitive customers/traffic buckets (3) manually add capacity via reserved burst nodes while warmup issues investigated.

mara: do it. I'll run manual scale and start throttles. owen, liam, coordinate on warmup failures. cody, prepare customer-facing note: "degraded streaming; mitigations in progress".

liam: digging into warmup-manager logs. root cause candidate: warmup job queue prioritization regress from recent rollout (eng-runtime v3.14) — warmup jobs are being deprioritized behind health checks causing many workers to fail readiness and requeue.

owen: confirming — we rolled a change that changed warmup concurrency defaults. Reverting would take ~25-30m incl canary, not great for immediate impact. We can do: bump pool-3 desired count +2 from control plane to absorb burst, plus enable burst capacity which doesn't require full warmup.

mara: run commands and post output here.

liam: paging opsbot to enable burst-cap. opsbot: please run `enable-burst pool-3`?

opsbot: runbook check OK. Executing: `redwoodctl capacity burst-enable --pool dedicated-prod-pool-3 --timeout 10m`

opsbot: success: burst capacity provisioned (+4 burst nodes, warmup bypass mode enabled). NOTE: burst nodes have limited caching; may increase p99 variance briefly.

mara: manually scaling desired: `redwoodctl capacity scale --pool dedicated-prod-pool-3 --delta +2`

opsbot: submitted scale request, status: ACTIVATING.

owen: enabling traffic fallback route for non-enterprise tag. route change (canary):
```
route.modify("/v1/stream", {
  filter: (req) => req.customer_tier != 'enterprise',
  target: 'hosted-fallback-v1'
})
```
Canary 10% now.

mara: throttling new streaming sessions to 0.6 concurrency per-API-key and rejecting > 5 minute sessions. Applying rate limit policy.

liam: metrics after actions (30s snapshot): queue depth -> 180, pool util -> 82%, p95 -> 900ms, p99 -> 2.4s. So mitigations working but still above target p99 500ms.

nina: customers on enterprise tier still impacted — they can't be routed to hosted. Any plan for enterprise?

owen: for enterprise customers we can spin a safety pool (cold) or temporarily re-route to compatible smaller model variant that uses less GPU mem but same API. Impact to quality but acceptable as emergency fallback. Need sign-off.

mara: do the model-fallback for enterprise as opt-in per-customer. cody coordinate with top customers.

cody: notified customers A/B/C that we may switch to fallback variant; asking for permission. One agrees; two prefer we try capacity first.

liam: warmup logs show queue starvation for warmup workers: warmup-manager backlog at ~600, many warmup jobs canceled after 40s. We should revert prioritization patch after hotfix. Creating PR to pin warmup concurrency to previous value.

nowen: hotfix plan: (1) revert warmup concurrency diff in runtime config, (2) restart warmup-manager on pool-3 with canary, (3) observe 2x warmup success rate. I can cut the revert and roll to pool-3 only. Estimated time 20-30m.

mara: ok. Proceed. liam, please keep surge controls active. cody, keep customers updated at T+15.

opsbot: hotfix deploy request accepted. `deploy hotfix/runtime-warmup-concurrency --target dedicated-prod-pool-3 --strategy canary --timeout 25m`

opsbot: canary step: apply to 10% of warmup-manager instances.

liam: canary logs show warmup success rate improved from 68% -> 94% on canary instances within 6 minutes.

nowen: promote hotfix to all pool-3 warmup-managers.

opsbot: promotion successful. warmup success rate trending to 92% cluster-wide. Queue depth dropping.

metrics snapshot (approx):
- p95: 520ms
- p99: 720ms
- queue depth: 42
- streaming aborts: down 80% from peak

mara: still above SLO p99 500ms but much improved. Recommend keep burst nodes until next maintenance window, keep throttles and fallback in place for 30m observation.

nina: preparing CS update to affected customers: short note + ETA for next update 30m. cody, send draft?

cody: draft posted to #customer-comms: "We're currently mitigated; streaming performance improved after scaling and a hotfix. We're monitoring and will follow up with timeline. Apologize for the disruption."

mara: handoff to next oncall in 30m. @owen will remain on-call for runtime until warmup metrics stable. @liam keep an eye on autoscaler logs. opsbot, keep auto-remediation runbook toggles recorded.

opsbot: incident log note: actions_taken=[manual_scale:+2, burst_enable:+4, throttles:enabled, route_canary:10%, fallback_variant:enabled_for_optin, hotfix:revert-warmup-concurrency]. All changes reversible.

nowen: postmortem action items (quick capture):
- revert change that altered warmup prioritization (done)
- add stronger canary gating for warmup concurrency changes (todo)
- improve autoscaler visibility when warmup jobs failing (todo)
- add emergency fallback to safely route enterprise to degraded-variant (todo)
- run chaos / load test for burst-warmup path (todo)

mara: closing notes: incident severity: P2 (SLO degradation affecting multiple customers), duration ~36m from pager -> stabilized. Will open incident ticket with timeline and owners for postmortem.

cody: sent customer updates to affected accounts. will follow up after postmortem.

nina: thanks team. I'll monitor CS queue.

mara: handing off to @liam for next 30m watch. if metrics hold we'll demote incident.

liam: watching. current p99 610ms and trending down.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: mitigation successful. Final status: p99 reduced to <800ms; warmup success restored. Incident closed to watch state at 1943210360."
